title: Make the RepoGround raw-call producer handoff immutable
goal: Replace the mutable dictionary handoff between AST call collection and resolution with a frozen slotted internal record while preserving the exact public v1 call-graph artifact, resolution semantics and deterministic goldset output.

approval.note: Only the call-graph producer and its focused test may change. Public artifact fields, schema/version values, resolution rules and unrelated cleanup are excluded.

acceptance.assertion: The collector stores each pending call in a frozen slotted typed record containing validated source positions, the AST callee expression and an immutable scope-frame tuple; the resolver accepts that record without dictionary-key access.

The unchanged 13-category Python call-graph goldset still emits 16 call records, zero skipped files and the canonical normalized payload SHA-256 647bb16d23b01a9318ed8b9c2ec31f3f122e5d0d7a631244439718ff9efec3ae before and after the refactor.

A focused regression proves the pending-call handoff cannot be mutated, and the existing Python call-graph, goldset and impact-index suites pass without changing public artifact fields or resolution expectations.

The patch changes exactly merger/repoground/architecture/call_graph.py and merger/repoground/tests/test_python_call_graph.py, introduces no Ruff C901 regression and does not mix producer behavior changes, dependency upgrades or repository-wide formatting.
Ruff, focused tests, full non-browser and browser suites, CodeQL, workflow contracts, revision-bound self-review, merge and remote-main readback pass on the exact final head.

metadata.scope_revision_reason: The 2026-07-15 Lenskit-wide task was remeasured on current RepoGround main. No C901 producer finding remains; the smallest still-valid decomposition is the mutable raw-call dictionary boundary.
does_not_establish: permission to change files outside the exact two-path scope
merge readiness before fresh CI and review
